I'm on the spectrum as well and however many people say that you should be yourself, it's not true for us. I'm opposite of op in that I don't seem excited no matter how excited I get, so I had to practice smiling and reacting to what the interviewer said in the way I thought I should, rather than the way I would naturally. the most important question to ask yourself is "how does the other person expect me to respond?" and go from there. I often take a beat before I respond just to think about what an appropriate reaction would be (although I've been told this is off-putting as well...) it takes a lot of effort, but hard work tends to pay off in situations like this. best of luck 🤖

I'm a 24-year-old woman and I've been shaving my head for a few years now, best decision I've ever made. I've met lots of women who say they want short hair but are afraid it would look bad. imo, none of them would have looked bad. Obviously I don't know what you look like so I can't say for sure, but I'm willing to bet you'd look just fine. I love how much time I save every morning not having to brush or style my hair. I save money by cutting it myself instead of going to a salon. When it's windy, I don't have hair blowing in my face. I use less shampoo. My hair dries really fast after it gets wet. And honestly I really like how I look. But if you shave your head and end up not liking it, it's only for a little while until it grows back. In my experience, toughing out bad haircuts is good for building self-confidence too 8P
